_comment: Grid B: (z, p_T^2), per pi0, HAND-CHOSEN edges (2026-10-28). Inside 0.3 < z < 1.0 and 0 < pT2 < 1.5 GeV2 the edges are EXACTLY those of the CLAS6 pi0 multiplicity-ratio paper (Mineeva et al., arXiv:2406.04513, Tables I/II; analysis note Table 3.9): z = 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 1.0 and pT2 = 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 0.55, 0.75, 1.5. Extra bins OUTSIDE that region, kept if statistics allow: z 0-0.1, 0.1-0.2, 0.2-0.3 and pT2 1.5-10. To change them, edit the edges below and rerun Stages B-D; Stage A does not depend on the grid. Keep the CLAS6 edges inside the list so those bins stay matched.
_bin_convention: Every bin is half-open [lo, hi) EXCEPT that a value exactly on the top edge lands in the LAST bin (Grid1D::find). The top edges here are 1.0 (z, the physical limit, z < 1 is cut) and 10 GeV2 (pT2, above the sample maximum of ~8.2 GeV2).

provenance.source: manual: z and pT2 edges of Mineeva et al. (CLAS EG2 pi0), arXiv:2406.04513 Appendix B, and analysis note v16 (2020-07-13) Table 3.9, plus extra bins outside their region
provenance._comment: n_events is 0 because the edges were chosen by hand, not computed from data. The 'manual' source tells the loaders this is NOT a placeholder grid.
